author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A specialty directory lists every specialty the clinic knows, under its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it. All specialties render on one page. The page is reachable by its own address alone.
acceptance_criteria: Requesting GET /specialties.html serves the specialty directory; the page is reachable by that address alone.
Every specialty the clinic knows is listed, under its stored name, unchanged in case and wording.
Each veterinarian under a specialty is shown by full name: first name then last name (for example "Helen Leary").
A veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page; the page lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
All specialties render on one page: no pagination and no paging control.
A specialty that no veterinarian holds is still listed, with no veterinarians under it.
Specialties, and the veterinarians under each, appear in a stable order across repeated requests.
Every piece of user-facing wording new to the page is present in all eleven message bundles and none is hard-coded into the page (REQ-LANG-002).
The page carries the standard navigation to owner search and to the veterinarian directory, as every page does (REQ-SYS-001).
non_goals: No navigation entry and no link to the page from any other page; a visible entry point may come as a follow-up request.
No managing of veterinarians or their specialties through the application; NG-2 is unchanged.
No searching or filtering of specialties, consistent with NG-9.
No pagination of the specialty directory.
notes: REQ-ID mapping: this handoff keeps req_id REQ-SPECIALTYDIRECTORY-001 as recorded in the intake, for pipeline continuity. The PRD-facing tag is REQ-VET-003, added to the renamed "Veterinarian and specialty directory" section of docs/prd.md, with anchor prd.md#req-vet-003. REQ-VET-003 is the next free number in the VET area (REQ-VET-002 is withdrawn to the Superseded list). Every downstream artifact that cites a PRD requirement cites REQ-VET-003. | Provenance: REQ-VET-003 is marked "(requested 2026-08-15)" in the PRD; the derived-brief blockquote now explains that mark. | Non-Goals table untouched, so no scope_overrides is due; NG-2 stands as the owner recorded. | Narrowest readings taken where the request was silent, per the dispatch: a stable presentation order (PRD edge case 4, mirroring the existing edge case 1); a specialty with no holders is still listed (edge case 3); specialty and veterinarian names are stored data, presented untranslated (edge case 5). | Two open questions recorded in the PRD rather than consulted: whether the page should get a visible entry point, and which particular ordering it should use. | The exact route is deliberately absent from docs/prd.md (mechanism); it is carried here and belongs in system-design.md#contracts. | Ubiquitous language: "Specialty directory" added to docs/ubiquitous-language.md before drafting.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty directory (PRD tag REQ-VET-003) lives in the existing vet feature package and uses only patterns already in force: Spring Data repository, web controller, Thymeleaf page. The new ground is the read path. Vet maps the vet-specialty relationship one way, so no existing repository can reach a specialty that no veterinarian holds, which acceptance criterion 6 requires. Three contracts are added and recorded in system-design.md#contracts: SpecialtyRepository (every specialty in name order, mirroring PetTypeRepository), SpecialtyDirectory (an immutable value object pairing each specialty with its holders), and SpecialtyController (the unpaged page on its own route). The pairing sits in SpecialtyDirectory rather than in the controller because the Web controller row of architecture-principles.md admits no rule, and the existing controller deviation does not extend to new rules. The rejected alternatives - an inverse association on Specialty, and a join query - are recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-15-specialty-directory-in-memory-projection.md. Vocabulary: 'Specialty directory' is the canonical term in ubiquitous-language.md, so SpecialtyDirectory is the domain-noun name the naming table prescribes.
integration_points: GET /specialties.html is the page address; it is the mechanism the PRD deliberately omits and is fixed here. No query parameter, no paging control.
SpecialtyRepository is a new Spring Data interface over the existing specialties table. No schema change, no data.sql change, on any of the three vendors.

SpecialtyDirectory is assembled from SpecialtyRepository plus the existing VetRepository.findAll(). Vet.specialties is EAGER, so nothing lazy escapes the transaction - spring.jpa.open-in-view is disabled.

The page uses fragments/layout.html and therefore carries the standard navigation (REQ-SYS-001). Pass a menu name that matches no existing menuItem, so no tab highlights and no navigation entry is added - the recorded non-goal.

Wording: messages.properties already carries specialties, vets, name and none. Reuse them and the eleven bundles need no edit. Any genuinely new wording goes into all eleven, enforced by I18nPropertiesSyncTest (REQ-LANG-002).
Vet, Specialty and the /vets serialized route are unchanged. Specialty gains no collection.

patterns.description: Lookup-value repository returning every row in name order via an explicit JPQL ORDER BY. SpecialtyRepository follows this shape; it takes no @Cacheable.
Package-private @Controller, constructor-injected repository, model attributes plus a view name. SpecialtyController follows this, without the pagination helper.
Page structure: layout fragment replacement, th:text message keys, th:each over the model list. specialtyList.html follows it minus the paging block.
Value object row - immutable, equality by value, no identity. SpecialtyDirectory realizes it with a static factory taking the two collections and returning the assembled directory.

risks.risk: VetRepository.findAll() is @Cacheable(vets) with no eviction configured, so the directory inherits vet-cache staleness (system-design.md open question 5).
risks.mitigation: Accept unchanged: the vet directory already reads through that cache and the application has no vet write path (NG-2). Do not add a second cache on SpecialtyRepository.

risks.risk: Stable order is required by acceptance criterion 7, but the PRD leaves the particular order open.
risks.mitigation: Narrowest reading: specialties by name from the repository ORDER BY; holders within a specialty by last name then first name, applied in SpecialtyDirectory. Both are asserted in the projection unit test, so the choice is visible if the owner later fixes a different one.

risks.risk: Both tables are read in full per request.
risks.mitigation: Bounded by the seeded data and by the no-pagination requirement. The ADR records the query-side change a larger clinic would need.

risks.risk: Adding the route to VetController would force a second @MockitoBean into VetControllerTests and mix two unrelated surfaces in one @WebMvcTest slice.
risks.mitigation: Separate SpecialtyController and SpecialtyControllerTests, matching the owner/pet/visit precedent of one controller per surface within a feature package.

risks.risk: An implementer may add a menuItem to fragments/layout.html to make the page reachable.
risks.mitigation: Explicit non-goal: the page is reached by its address alone. layout.html is read-only for this slice.

notes: Deviation from the prd-entry file_targets, deliberate and scope-neutral: the controller and its test are SpecialtyController / SpecialtyControllerTests rather than edits to VetController / VetControllerTests. Placement is a design call; the acceptance criteria and the five prd-entry test names are unchanged and all five belong in SpecialtyControllerTests. SpecialtyDirectoryTests is an addition, not a substitution. | Security: the slice adds a read-only GET with no request parameter and no new trust boundary. Stored names render through Thymeleaf default escaping (threat-model XSS row). No authentication is added and none is removed - the recorded posture is unchanged. | Fail-closed: an empty specialties table yields an empty page, not an error. | Open questions taken at their narrowest and left recorded rather than consulted, per the dispatch: (1) the presentation order - name order for specialties, last-then-first name for holders, recorded in PRD open questions; (2) a visible entry point - none, recorded in PRD open questions; (3) whether SpecialtyDirectory should expose a nested element type or a map - left to the implementer, since the domain vocabulary names the directory but not its element. | Durable memory written this dispatch: docs/adr/2026-08-15-specialty-directory-in-memory-projection.md (new, indexed in docs/adr/README.md) and docs/system-design.md (package tree line, three Contracts rows marked designed-not-yet-built, REQ-VET-003 added to the Vet, Specialty and VetRepository rows, one invariant sentence). | ubiquitous-language.md needed no edit: the product expert added 'Specialty directory' before this triage. | No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is empty. | Basis for the covering-pattern claims: grep and direct reads of the vet and owner packages; the IntelliJ oracle is not connected in this run, so the resolution basis is the weaker textual one.

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: SpecialtyController mirrors VetController's package-private class / public constructor / constructor-injection shape exactly
SpecialtyDirectory realizes the value-object rule: record, compact-constructor List.copyOf defensive copies on both the outer directory and the nested SpecialtyHolders, no mutable state
SpecialtyRepository mirrors PetTypeRepository's lookup-repository shape: explicit JPQL ORDER BY, @Transactional(readOnly = true), no @Cacheable, javadoc explains the intentional read-only scope
Naming is clear and unabbreviated throughout (holdersOf, BY_LAST_THEN_FIRST_NAME, SpecialtyHolders); no get/set prefixes on record accessors
specialtyList.html mirrors vetList.html's th:each/th:if none-fallback pattern precisely, keeping the two directory pages visually and structurally consistent
./gradlew checkFormat and compileJava both pass clean on the working tree

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Unbounded read (low, not weaker than baseline): the endpoint loads every specialty and every vet with EAGER-fetched specialties, unpaged, and joins them in memory at O(specialties x vets x specialties-per-vet). The existing /vets JSON endpoint already performs an unpaged full-table read, so this matches the baseline rather than degrading it; if the clinic dataset ever grows beyond demonstration size, this route and /vets should be bounded together.

Supply chain not verified against the NVD in this review: build.gradle is untouched by the change set (no new or upgraded dependency), and the project configures no OWASP dependency-check plugin, so no NVD match ran here. Spring Boot 4.1.0 CVE status remains unverified by this pass and should be closed by CI or a human.
approved_aspects: XSS: specialtyList.html renders every request-visible value through th:text (escaped) and uses no th:utext and no __${...}__ preprocessing; it mirrors vetList.html's escaping pattern exactly, so the one-way-per-concern rule holds
Injection into data access: SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties uses a constant JPQL @Query with no interpolation and no request-derived value; the endpoint takes no request parameter at all

Exposed surface: /specialties.html is a single read-only GET that mutates nothing and exposes only specialty names and vet names already public at /vets.html and /vets, so it does not widen the baseline in docs/system-design.md Security Context
Least privilege at the data layer: SpecialtyRepository extends the marker Repository interface and exposes exactly one read method, granting no write or delete surface for Specialty
Mass assignment: no request-bound type is introduced, so no identifier-binding disallow list is owed

Immutability and thread safety: SpecialtyDirectory and SpecialtyHolders are records that defensively copy their lists via List.copyOf in compact constructors; the singleton controller holds only injected repositories and no mutable state
Fail-secure identity handling: SpecialtyDirectory.holds returns false for a specialty with a null id, so an unsaved instance cannot draw the whole vet roster under it

No shell execution, file I/O, deserialization config, reflection, randomness, secrets, or logging is introduced anywhere in the change (grep over the new vet package sources for Runtime/ProcessBuilder/exec/Files./FileWriter/JsonTypeInfo/enableDefaultTyping//tmp/ returns nothing)

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldShowEachHolderByFullName asserts containsString("Helen Leary") and containsString("Rafael Ortega"), but the source names live only as inline string literals in the unrelated clinicKnowsThreeSpecialtiesAndThreeVeterinarians @BeforeEach (createVetHolding("Helen","Leary",...)). The expected full name is retyped rather than derived from the same source, violating testing-principles.md's Derived Expectations and Three-Tier Data Naming (a Tier-1 meaningful value needs a role-describing constant, not a duplicated literal). If the fixture first/last name ever changes, the assertion silently stops verifying what its name claims.
findings.fix: Introduce named constants for the two specialty-holder names (e.g. RADIOLOGY_HOLDER_FIRST_NAME/LAST_NAME, SURGERY_HOLDER_FIRST_NAME/LAST_NAME) analogous to the existing HOLDS_NO_SPECIALTY_FIRST_NAME/LAST_NAME pair, use them in the @BeforeEach fixture, and build the expected full-name assertion from the same constants (e.g. RADIOLOGY_HOLDER_FIRST_NAME + " " + RADIOLOGY_HOLDER_LAST_NAME) instead of a fresh literal.

findings.description: SpecialtyDirectory.holds() has a documented defensive branch - a specialty with a null id (getId() == null) is treated as held by nobody rather than by everybody, per the method's own Javadoc. JaCoCo (build/reports/jacoco/test/html/org.springframework.samples.petclinic.vet/SpecialtyDirectory.java.html) shows this branch (return false; at line 76) as never executed by any test in SpecialtyDirectoryTests or SpecialtyControllerTests. The behavior is deliberate and explained in the code, but nothing in the suite would fail if it regressed (e.g. to 'null id matches everyone').
findings.fix: Add a case to SpecialtyDirectoryTests, e.g. theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldTreatAnUnsavedSpecialtyAsHeldByNobody, that builds a Specialty via createSpecialty(name) but leaves its id unset (or a variant factory createAnUnsavedSpecialty(name)), pairs it with a veterinarian holding specialties generally, and asserts the resulting SpecialtyHolders.veterinarians() is empty.

approved_aspects: All five prd-entry test names present in SpecialtyControllerTests and each exercises the acceptance criterion its name names.

SpecialtyDirectoryTests is a true unit suite (no Spring context) covering the ordering and immutability rules the design pushed into the value object, correctly widening the pyramid's unit base per testing-principles.md's 'ratio moves when logic moves'.
Line coverage on the new classes is 96-100% (SpecialtyDirectory 96%, SpecialtyController 100%, SpecialtyHolders 100%), above the 80% brief target.
Four-phase structure held throughout, no phase comments or narration; AssertJ used fluently (satisfiesExactly, singleElement().satisfies, containsExactly) with no JUnit assertEquals/assertTrue.
Construction is behind createSpecialty/createVetHolding factory methods in both files, consistent with the file's own conventions and the sibling VetControllerTests pattern already in the codebase.

Mocking stays within the brief: @MockitoBean on the two repositories plus MockMvc mirrors the existing VetControllerTests idiom the brief tolerates; SpecialtyDirectoryTests uses only real value objects.
Edge cases 1, 3 and 4 from prd.md (stable order, an unheld specialty still listed, stable presentation order) each have a dedicated test with real assertions, not invented data.
./gradlew test is green for both new test classes; the full gradle test task also passes.

Carried forward from round 1: supply chain still not verified against the NVD. build.gradle is untouched by the change set (whole-diff file list carries no build file), the project configures no OWASP dependency-check plugin, and this reviewer has no network access, so no NVD match ran in either round. Spring Boot 4.1.0 CVE status remains unverified and should be closed by CI or a human.
approved_aspects: Fix delta since the round-1 basis tree (719d850b) touches three files only - docs/prd.md, SpecialtyControllerTests.java, SpecialtyDirectoryTests.java. No production Java, no Thymeleaf template, no build or configuration file changed, so no new attack surface was introduced and the round-1 threat-model walk over SpecialtyController, SpecialtyDirectory, SpecialtyRepository and specialtyList.html still holds verbatim.

docs/prd.md delta is a single link line adding a relative in-repo ADR link (adr/2026-08-15-specialty-directory-in-memory-projection.md). Relative path, no remote URL, no javascript:/data: scheme, target file exists in the change set.

SpecialtyControllerTests delta replaces two inline fixture literals with four private static final String name constants and builds the expected full name from the same constants. The values are fictional veterinarian names from the demonstration dataset, not credentials; a secret-name sweep over the delta (token, password, secret, key, credential) returns nothing.

SpecialtyDirectoryTests delta adds createAnUnsavedSpecialty plus theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldTreatAnUnsavedSpecialtyAsHeldByNobody, which now pins the fail-secure branch SpecialtyDirectory.holds uses for a null-id specialty. This strengthens the security posture: the deliberate 'unsaved specialty is held by nobody, not by everybody' behavior is now regression-protected rather than only documented.

Detection-pattern sweep re-run over the whole change set for Runtime, ProcessBuilder, exec(, Files., FileWriter, FileOutputStream, JsonTypeInfo, enableDefaultTyping and /tmp/ returns nothing; no shell execution, file I/O, deserialization configuration, reflection, randomness or logging is introduced anywhere.
No test writes outside the build tree and none uses system /tmp; both new test classes construct in-memory value objects only.

author: change-grader

blast_radius.note: Eleven files in one module: four new vet-package files plus a template, two new test classes, and additive doc edits. No existing production Java is modified, no build, config, schema or message-bundle file is touched, and no sensitive path is in the diff, so the only runtime reach is one new GET route.

semantic_surprise.note: Every hunk read: the code does exactly what the PRD entry says. The subtle decisions are deliberate, documented and pinned by tests - a null-id specialty is held by nobody rather than everybody, the record constructor copies both lists, and holders sort by last then first name. One cosmetic residue worth an eyeball: multiple holders in a cell are space-separated with no delimiter, so two holders render as 'Helen Leary Adam Leary'; that copies the vetList idiom and no test pins the separator.

test_adequacy.note: Tests exercise the changed behavior rather than restate it. The directory tests cover pairing, an unheld specialty, an unsaved specialty, a vet holding nothing, holder ordering, given-order preservation and defensive copying; the controller tests drive real MVC and Thymeleaf rendering and carry negative assertions (no self-link in the navigation, no paging control, the specialty-less vet absent) that would fail against a broken implementation.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four planned reviewers approved in round 2 with zero findings, but the security reviewer carried two recommendations forward unchanged: the route loads every specialty and every vet unpaged and joins them in memory, and Spring Boot 4.1.0 has no NVD check in either round because the reviewer had no network and the project configures no dependency-check plugin.

scope_deviation.note: The change matches the recorded owner request line for line - own address, no navigation entry or link, unpaged, full names, specialty-less vets omitted - with zero consultations and zero build retries after the gate. The single design revision was a bookkeeping supersede adding docs/adr/README.md to the covered paths, not a redirect of the design.

rationale: Read every hunk: a contained, additive feature that matches its request and is well tested. Nothing in the code needs a second look. Before merging, decide on the two carried-forward security recommendations - the unpaged full read of both tables, and the unverified Spring Boot 4.1.0 CVE status - since neither is closed here.
